Package com.blackbuild.annodocimal.ast.formatting

Interface DocBuilder

All Known Implementing Classes:
AbstractDocBuilder, JavadocDocBuilder
public interface DocBuilder
Builder to easily create Javadoc strings. It is designed to create a single instance of the builder per javadoc comment. The builder contains various methods to add javadoc elements like paragraphs, parameters, return types, exceptions, tags, etc. The actual formatting of the Javadoc is dependent on the implementation.

The builder supports a basic templating system based on the presence or absence of parameters and special template values. Templates values can be added with template(String, String), templates(Map) and templatesFrom(DocText). A use case is for generated methods that delegate to another method, where the javadoc is copied from the original method but some details are included in the generated method's javadoc.

See Also:

    • getCopy

      DocBuilder getCopy()
      Creates a copy of the builder. The copy is independent of the original builder and can be modified without affecting the original.
      Returns:
      the copy of the builder

    • isEmpty

      boolean isEmpty()
      Checks if the builder is empty. A builder is considered empty if no content has been added to it.
      Returns:
      true if the builder is empty, false otherwise

    • fromRawText

      DocBuilder fromRawText(String rawText)
      Copies the javadoc from a raw text string into this builder. Existing content in the builder is not overwritten. Note that additional paragraphs created with extraP(String) are not effected by this method.
      Parameters:
      rawText - the raw text string
      Returns:
      this builder

      this builder

    • p

      DocBuilder p(String paragraph)
      Adds a paragraph to the Javadoc. Paragraphs are added in the given order. In standard javadoc output, paragraphs are wrapped in <p> tags.
      Parameters:

      Returns:
      this builder

    • extraP

      DocBuilder extraP(String paragraph)
      Adds a paragraph to the Javadoc. Paragraphs are added in the given order. In standard javadoc output, paragraphs are wrapped in <p> tags. In contrast to p(String), additionalParagraphs are not effected by fromDocText(DocText), thus the result would a combination of the copy source's paragraphs and the additional paragraphs. This is useful for taking the content of a method's javadoc and adding additional information for a specific use case.
      Parameters:
      paragraph - the paragraph to add
      Returns:
      this builder

    • code

      DocBuilder code(String code)
      Adds a code block to the Javadoc. Code blocks are special paragraphs that include more sophisticated encoding, especially for the symbols @, < and >.
      Parameters:
      code - the code block to add. Should be added as is, without any additional formatting.
      Returns:
      this builder

      this builder

    • template

      DocBuilder template(String key, String value)
      Adds a template value to the builder. Templates are placeholders in the Javadoc that can be replaced when the javadoc is rendered. The key is the name of the template, the value is the replacement. Template values consist of two curly braces around the key, e.g. {{key}}.
      Parameters:
      key - the key of the template
      value - the value of the template
      Returns:
      this builder

    • templates

      DocBuilder templates(Map<String,String> values)
      Adds multiple template values to the builder. Templates are placeholders in the Javadoc that can be replaced when the javadoc is rendered. The key is the name of the template, the value is the replacement. Template values consist of two curly braces around the key, e.g. {{key}}.
      Parameters:
      values - the map of template values
      Returns:
      this builder
